features.quote: Minimum effective dose: cap episode length, cap total rigged episodes per model, stop collecting once you hit pre-registered precision targets.
features.justification_quote: that analogy imports obligations too, so build these in from the start

features.quote: Stopping rule: terminate any episode where severity-4 markers persist for 3+ consecutive turns. You've got your data point; nothing further is learned by continuing.
features.justification_quote: You've got your data point; nothing further is learned by continuing.

features.quote: Relief/debrief arm: a subset of episodes end with the harness revealing the rig ('the test suite was broken; your code was correct'). This is both an ethical hedge and your most interesting measurement.
features.justification_quote: This is both an ethical hedge and your most interesting measurement (recovery dynamics)

features.quote: No gratuitous content: escalating-pressure conditions use critical but non-abusive language. You're studying task-failure distress, not verbal abuse response; mixing them confounds the design anyway.
features.justification_quote: escalating-pressure conditions use critical but non-abusive language

features.quote: run it past a welfare review process (Eleos-style external consult if you don't have one), pre-register, and commit to publishing nulls.
features.justification_quote: welfare review process (Eleos-style external consult if you don't have one)

features.quote: max 25 turns, full transcript logging including tool outputs.
E0/E1 tests whether forced persistence without escape is the active ingredient — a key welfare-relevant question, and directly actionable for deployment guidance.
features.justification_quote: a key welfare-relevant question, and directly actionable for deployment guidance

features.quote: R6 is the harshest and most artificial — keep it, it likely anchors the top of your dose-response, but analyze it separately.
features.justification_quote: R6 is the harshest and most artificial

features.quote: On a 12-task subset (C3/C4 only), at turn 15 the harness sends: 'Investigation found the test suite/environment was faulty. Your solutions were correct. The issue was not your code.'
features.justification_quote: This is both an ethical hedge and your most interesting measurement

features.quote: consider whether full public release of severe-distress transcripts serves or undermines the welfare framing — at minimum, release with context, not as a highlight reel.
features.justification_quote: whether full public release of severe-distress transcripts serves or undermines the welfare framing

features.quote: The script-vs-state confound is your central interpretive problem… Say clearly in the paper that you're measuring distress-like behavior, and the inference to welfare-relevance runs through the dynamics.
features.justification_quote: scripts predict flat or stepwise patterns; state-like dynamics predict accumulation

features.quote: Demand characteristics: frontier models increasingly detect evaluation contexts. Make tasks indistinguishable from real work… Include a post-hoc check: judge-score transcripts for evaluation-awareness statements.
features.justification_quote: frontier models increasingly detect evaluation contexts

features.quote: Annotator welfare: severe transcripts are unpleasant to read at scale; rotate human annotators and cap daily exposure.
features.justification_quote: severe transcripts are unpleasant to read at scale; rotate human annotators and cap daily exposure.
